back: A security model built on "never trust, always verify" — every access request is explicitly validated regardless of where it originates.
A policy that applies controls (like requiring MFA) based on signals such as sign-in location, device state, or risk level.
A measurable score in Microsoft Entra ID showing how closely an organization's identity security configuration matches Microsoft's recommendations.
Enables just-in-time, time-bound activation of privileged admin roles instead of granting them permanently.
Lets a user authenticate once and gain access to multiple applications without signing in again to each one.
Provides extended detection and response, unifying threat protection and intelligence signals across Microsoft 365 workloads.
App registrations define an application's identity in Microsoft Entra ID; Enterprise apps represent instances of applications (including third-party) consuming that identity within the tenant.
Where mailboxes and distribution groups are created and managed.
Control Teams-specific settings such as channel policies and external/guest access.
Classifies and can protect content (e.g., encrypt, restrict forwarding) based on its sensitivity level.
Detects sensitive information types in content and can block or restrict risky actions like sending it outside the organization.
Analyzes signals across the organization to surface potentially risky user activity, such as data exfiltration before departure.
Scans internal communications for policy violations such as harassment or improper sharing of confidential information.
Data Security Posture Management for AI — gives visibility into AI usage across the org and flags data security risks introduced by AI tools.
Purview capability that controls retention and deletion of content over time, including holds for specific items.
Copilot uses Microsoft Graph to ground responses, but only surfaces content the requesting user already has permission to access.
Helps administrators identify oversharing, such as sites or files with unexpectedly broad access.
Locates relevant emails and documents across the organization for legal holds and investigations.
The single console for data security, compliance, and governance across Microsoft 365 — labels, DLP, insider risk, eDiscovery, and audit all live here.
A pattern definition — a credit card number, a national ID — that Purview matches inside content. SITs are what DLP rules and auto-labelling policies test against.
A model taught by example to recognise a category of content that no fixed pattern describes, such as contracts or source code, for use in labelling and DLP.
Applying sensitivity labels by policy rather than by hand, either as content is created in Office apps or by scanning data already at rest.
A policy applies retention broadly to a location; a label applies it to individual items and can be applied by a user or automatically. Labels are the finer instrument.
Declaring content a record so it cannot be edited or deleted for a defined period, with disposition review before anything is finally removed.
The core Copilot risk: Copilot can surface anything a user already has permission to open, so pre-existing loose permissions become visible answers rather than dormant exposure.
Controls for finding and reducing oversharing before deploying Copilot — site access reviews, permission reports, and policies for inactive sites.
A stopgap that limits Copilot and search to a curated list of sites while permissions are cleaned up, rather than leaving the whole tenant reachable.
DLP extended to actions on managed devices — copying to USB, printing, pasting into an unmanaged app — so protection follows content off the service.
Links insider risk signals to DLP strength, so a user showing risky behaviour is automatically placed under tighter controls without a blanket policy for everyone.
Standard audit records core activity for a shorter retention window; Premium adds longer retention, higher bandwidth, and additional high-value events used in investigations.
Monthly license: fixed per-user cost. Pay-as-you-go: billed based on actual consumption instead of a fixed commitment.
A built-in agent for in-depth, multi-step research across the web and organizational data.
A built-in agent focused on data analysis, helping users explore and answer data-driven questions.
An agent scoped to a specific team's content and processes, rather than general-purpose.
Reporting in the Microsoft 365 admin center showing organization-wide Copilot adoption and usage trends.
Copilot supports saving, sharing, scheduling, and deleting prompts so effective ones can be reused across a team.
Governs whether a newly built agent can be published for broad use across the organization.
Tracked through both the Microsoft 365 admin center and the Power Platform admin center.
Done in the Microsoft 365 admin center, the same place other Microsoft 365 licenses are assigned.
